test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following numbers is NOT prime?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To check if a number **N** is prime, test its divisibility by prime numbers up to **√N**.

For **817**, √817 ≈ **28.5**. Test primes: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19...

Check 19: 817 ÷ 19 = **43**.

Since 817 is divisible by 19 and 43, it is **not a prime number**.

**∴ The correct answer is 817.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given numbers:** 811, 313, 817, 317

**Definition:** A **prime number** has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. A **composite number** has more than two factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/859b504c3fb4fce9a6c6696e279da4fc927f23e4a64c54581bb8363cf3dc2ec7.png] 

Evaluating each option:

⇒ **811:** Not divisible by primes up to 28 (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23). It is **prime**.

⇒ **313:** Not divisible by primes up to 17 (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17). It is **prime**.

⇒ **317:** Not divisible by primes up to 17 (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17). It is **prime**.

⇒ **817:** 817 ÷ 19 = 43. Since it has factors 1, 19, 43, and 817, it is **not prime**.

**∴ The correct answer is 817.**

**__Additional Information__**

Primality Test

To determine if a number N is prime, check for factors among prime numbers up to √N. If no such factor exists, N is prime.

Composite Numbers

A positive integer greater than 1 that has at least one divisor other than 1 and itself is called a **composite number**.

Key Primes

Numbers like 817 (19 × 43) and 221 (13 × 17) are common exam trap numbers that appear prime but are actually composite.</p
